name: 100 gecs
label: Dog Show / Atlantic
lede: Two St. Louis kids, one Chicago tree, and a debut album that started as a joke about a Minecraft festival and ended up rewriting what a pop record was allowed to sound like.

eras.title: Two laptops, two cities
eras.text: Dylan Brady and Laura Les met as friends of friends in the St. Louis suburbs, then spent years making music apart: he in beat-scene SoundCloud and label EPs, she as osno1. The duo started as file swaps between Los Angeles and Chicago.

q: I was so intimidated by how good he was.
years.src: The FADER: The brilliant pop anarchy · Kerrang
years.h: Laura Les meets Dylan Brady at a house party outside St. Louis
years.p: Both grew up in the suburbs (Brady in Kirkwood, Les in Webster Groves). Her first reaction was to go home and work on music.
years.xp: The FADER has Les describing the meeting: they were friends of friends at a St. Louis-area house party in 2012, and she left feeling outclassed. Kerrang adds that they'd been circling the same Missouri scene for years, down to both being at a Van Halen reunion show without knowing each other.

years.h: Dylan Brady's solo debut All I Ever Wanted
years.p: Brady had been posting electronic hip-hop productions to SoundCloud while studying audio engineering. He also played in a band called Cake Pop, whose EP came out the same year.

years.src: Wikipedia: 100 gecs · Wikipedia: Laura Les · Wikipedia: Dylan Brady
years.h: The first gecs songs get made in Laura Les's Chicago apartment
years.p: They traded Logic Pro sessions, each finishing what the other started. Les later called the method an exquisite corpse.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the start of 100 gecs to winter 2015, in Les's Chicago apartment, with Logic files passed back and forth. Les has described it as very much an improv mentality: write songs they'd want to listen to. Other Wikipedia pages for the two members give 2016 as the founding year, so the start date is soft.

years.h: 100 gecs EP, self-released
years.p: The duo's first release, a year before either of them had a label. Les was also putting out records as osno1, including one about dead bodies.
years.xp: Les released the osno1 EP hello kitty skates to the fuckin CEMETARY in 2016, which she described as a bunch of songs about dead bodies. A follow-up, i just dont wanna name it anything with "beach" in the title, came in 2017, and she dropped the osno1 name in 2018.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dylan Brady · Wikipedia: Laura Les
years.h: Brady gets a Mad Decent EP; Les gets Vice's attention
years.p: Brady's Peace & Love came out on Mad Decent. Les's BIG SUMMER JAMS 2018 EP drew a Vice write-up calling it debauched digital celebrations.

eras.title: A closet, a parking lot, a pine tree
eras.text: Brady's Los Angeles and Les's Chicago closet produced 1000 gecs, mostly by email. It landed in the spring and turned into a year-end argument nobody could stop having.

years.h: "Money Machine" arrives two days before the album
years.p: Recorded in January 2019. Brady built the beat in Logic; Les says it struck her as sarcastic, with a bassline that seemed to be laughing at her.
years.xp: Wikipedia's account of the song: Les built her vocal from real-life frustration at work, borrowing the tone of a King of the Hill character, and Brady took the title from money he'd seen on the ground. Pitchfork ranked it No. 61 on its 2019 songs list and it later reached No. 47 on Billboard's Hot Rock and Alternative Songs.

q: I still work at my full time job in a restaurant.
years.src: Wikipedia: 1000 gecs · The FADER: The brilliant pop anarchy
years.h: 1000 gecs · Dog Show
years.p: Roughly 80 percent of it was made remotely, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork gave it 7.4 and called it one of the year's most fascinating, exhilarating experimental pop albums.
years.xp: Les recorded her vocals in her closet, pitch-shifted, which Wikipedia says she has tied to voice dysphoria. Brady and Les name John Zorn, Cannibal Corpse, YouTube and nightcore as reference points, and Brady called the record a best-of compilation. The FADER caught Les just after release still working a full-time restaurant job.

years.h: The "Money Machine" video: a parking lot, deep fried
years.p: Paper put it somewhere between a cybernetic hallucination and a deep fried meme. It was shot in the same Des Plaines office park as the album cover.

years.src: Wikipedia: 1000 gecs · Wikipedia: 1000 gecs and the Tree of Clues
years.h: Stems and a cappellas go up for free download
years.p: The duo released instrumentals and vocal stems of 1000 gecs, and the fan remixes started immediately.
years.xp: That release is what fed the remix album: Wikipedia says the follow-up was retitled in early 2020 after the duo found fan-made remixes of their stems.

years.src: Wikipedia: 100 gecs · The FADER: The brilliant pop anarchy
years.h: Fans find the album cover's tree on Google Maps
years.p: It's a pine in an office park in Des Plaines, Illinois. People started leaving offerings there.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports the tree stands at an Acuity Brands-owned office park near O'Hare, and that fans made pilgrimages and left items behind. The Chicago Tribune compared the phenomenon to the house on American Football's 1999 cover. The FADER noted fans found the coordinates, made memes, and started petitions.

years.h: Opening for Brockhampton on the Heaven Belongs to You tour
years.p: Wikipedia lists them as support on the 2019 run, alongside slowthai, plus six headline dates along the route.

years.h: A.G. Cook remixes "Money Machine"
years.p: The PC Music founder's take was an early entry in the remix wave that became the Tree of Clues album.

years.h: Performing in front of a green-screen aquarium on Adult Swim
years.p: On FishCenter Live they played "800db Cloud" and "Stupid Horse".

years.h: The New York Times names it the best album of 2019
years.p: Jon Caramanica put 1000 gecs at No. 1 on his list; Jon Pareles put it at No. 10. Pitchfork and Stereogum also listed it.
years.xp: Rolling Stone had already named them an Artist You Need to Know that year. Wikipedia credits the record with popularizing hyperpop as a mainstream idea.

eras.title: Remixes, a major label and a Euphoria needle drop
eras.text: With a whole scene remixing them, the duo signed to Atlantic, put out a remix album with Charli XCX and Fall Out Boy, and each stepped out on their own.

years.h: Charli XCX and Rico Nasty jump on the "Ringtone" remix
years.p: Kero Kero Bonito joined too. Brady had already co-produced Charli's "Click".
years.xp: Wikipedia says Umru teased the remix at a live DJ set on January 24, 2020. Pitchfork's Jillian Mapes said it recalled PC Music's work and predicted an internet hit; Paper called it a certified hit.

years.h: Atlantic signs 100 gecs
years.p: Brady said the ambition was to be as big as Ed Sheeran. The duo kept their own Dog Show label alongside the deal.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the Atlantic signing in 2020, and Brady's Ed Sheeran line is the quote it prints. 10,000 gecs, three years later, is credited to Dog Show and Atlantic together.

years.src: Wikipedia: 1000 gecs and the Tree of Clues
years.h: 1000 gecs and the Tree of Clues
years.p: The remix album debuted at No. 198 on the Billboard 200, their first chart entry. Injury Reserve, Charli XCX, Black Dresses and Fall Out Boy are on it.
years.xp: Metacritic has it at 81 from seven reviews. NME's Ben Jolley called it an exhilarating snapshot of pop's alternative future.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hand Crushed by a Mallet (remix)
years.h: Fall Out Boy's Patrick Stump sings on "Hand Crushed by a Mallet"
years.p: Pete Wentz proposed it; the duo got a zip file of Stump singing the intro. Craig Owens and Nicole Dollanganger took the verses and chorus.
years.xp: An animated video followed on August 20, 2020, directed by Dario Alva, and the song hit No. 23 on Billboard's Hot Rock and Alternative Songs.

years.h: Laura Les releases her solo single "Haunted"
years.p: It later appeared in season 2 of HBO's Euphoria and went RIAA Gold, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Pitchfork's cover story: This Is Your Brain on 100 gecs
years.p: The magazine gave the duo its cover two years after the debut.

years.h: "mememe" starts the 10,000 gecs era
years.p: The single arrived with a robed-wizard video, the first hint that the second album would be louder.

years.h: Terminal 5 closes out the first North American tour, streamed on Twitch
years.p: The autumn 2021 run was billed as the 10000 gecs tour, with Tony Velour, Underscores, Aaron Cartier and Alice Gas opening.

eras.title: Ten songs in the bin
eras.text: The second album took 18 months and a full restart. The finished record had a nu-metal opener, a drummer, and no nightcore pitch-shifting on Les's voice.

years.cap: 100 Gecs,ARGO-Konzerte,Arena Nürnberger Versicherungen,Dylan Brady,Konzert,Laura Les,Livekonzert,Livemusik,Orbit Stage,Rock im Park · Wikimedia
years.h: They play Coachella, a week after releasing "Doritos & Fritos"
years.p: The single was an alt-rock detour from their signature sound. The music video, released May 16, starred a Danny DeVito impersonator.
years.xp: The year also brought slots at BUKU, Ceremonia, Forecastle, Bonnaroo, Lollapalooza and Governors Ball, plus dates supporting Nine Inch Nails and My Chemical Romance in the US, per Wikipedia. Reading and Leeds came in August.

years.h: They scrap their first ten songs for the second album
years.p: The FADER has Les saying they thought they had the album, then decided to do something else. Later demo counts run as high as 6,000, per Kerrang.
years.xp: Les told The FADER that the major-label setting added pressure and that perfectionism was messing with her head. Brady told Kerrang the process had Darwin vibes, and only the strongest song survives.

q: If it sounds faithful, it's because it sounds good.
years.src: The FADER: 100 gecs discuss channeling · The FADER: 100 gecs, seriously · Kerrang
years.h: Recorded in the room where System of a Down made Toxicity
years.p: Brady ran an eight-string guitar through a Boss HM2 into a Dual Rectifier cabinet, and Josh Freese played real drums, per The FADER.
years.xp: Les moved to Los Angeles to work in person with Brady. She also took vocal lessons during the pandemic, and told Kerrang she wanted her pitch-shifting to be more a tool than a crutch.

years.h: Snake Eyes EP, with Skrillex on "Torture Me"
years.p: Three songs in 6:04. Pitchfork gave it a 5.6 and called it inconsequential; Rolling Stone said "Hey Big Man" had become a live staple.

years.h: "Hollywood Baby" is the last single before the album
years.p: Billboard, i-D, Pitchfork and Slant all put it on their 2023 best-songs lists.

years.src: Wikipedia: 10,000 gecs · Album of the Year: 10,000 gecs · BrooklynVegan: Pitchfork's Top 50
years.h: 10,000 gecs: Pitchfork gives it 8.2 and ranks it No. 18 of 2023
years.p: Nu-metal, ska and alt-funk in 26 minutes, on Dog Show and Atlantic.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's score was 8.2, per Wikipedia and Album of the Year, and its review called the record a reevaluation of the most declasse rock genres of the 2000s. Metacritic lists 81 from 15 critics. Year-end lists: Stereogum No. 10, NME No. 14, Exclaim! No. 12, Rolling Stone No. 74 of 100. It debuted at No. 59 on the Billboard 200. Reviews weren't uniform: Album of the Year lists the Evening Standard at 20 out of 100.

The cover shows a bridge in Orange, California, which drew less of a following than the tree.

years.src: Interview: 100 Gecs on Shit Posts · Wikipedia: 100 gecs
years.h: Machine Girl opens the biggest tour yet, with two nights at Brooklyn Mirage
years.p: Fans bring Game Boys and DS units to the pit, Les told Interview, though she now watches from the side with a big glass of beer.

eras.title: A Black Parade
eras.text: After the album cycle, the duo went back on the road with a band they had opened for three years earlier.

years.h: Long Live The Black Parade tour with My Chemical Romance
years.p: Wikipedia lists the duo on the bill of the 2025 run, after supporting the band's 2022 reunion shows.
